source.title: Scaling Convex Neural Networks with Burer-Monteiro Factorization
source.authors: Arda Sahiner; Tolga Ergen; Batu Mehmet Ozturkler; John Pauly; Morteza Mardani; Mert Pilanci

record.tranche_reason: The study trains BM-factorized gated-ReLU CNNs and includes training-accuracy curves on CIFAR-10, a different training formulation from the claim's standard convolutional networks.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy curves for the study's CIFAR-10 models bear on V1, but the text does not give their numerical values. The test-accuracy comparisons do not measure training error. The spiral-data experiment measures relative optimality gap, not classification error.
record.test_reason: Figure 5(a) reports training classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 for SGD-trained convolutional networks, bearing on V1 through a different, layerwise BM-factorized formulation. The supplied text omits the plotted values, so it cannot establish whether training error approaches zero.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: BM factorization makes greedy layerwise convex CNN training tractable and achieves test accuracy comparable to cited end-to-end ReLU networks. The authors also emphasize verifiable optimality bounds and empirical convergence to suboptimal saddle points.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR-10 experiment uses layerwise BM-factorized convex gated-ReLU CNNs, with m in [1, 2, 4], rather than the standard networks described in V1. The paper reports SGD and the training setup, but does not state the initialization for this experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Factor count m changes the reported test accuracy; training accuracy is shown by stage in Figure 5.

fits_no_version.finding: On spiral data, GD almost never reaches the regularized global optimum; the authors identify suboptimal saddle points and only a minor relationship between optimality gap and factor count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GD can converge to suboptimal stationary points in BM-factorized gated-ReLU networks even when all local minima are global. This does not measure V1's classification error or V2's teacher-student spurious local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper derives sufficient factor-count and rank conditions for global optimality of local minima in BM formulations, including sufficiently many heads in linear self-attention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient factorization size can eliminate spurious local minima in specified BM formulations; this is distinct from V2's ReLU teacher-student setting and width comparison.

record.problems: The relevant CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results are shown only in a figure, without textual numerical values or stated uncertainty. Initialization for this experiment is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 1's test-accuracy comparisons are excluded because they measure test accuracy, not the training classification error in V1. The spiral-data results in Figure 2 measure relative optimality gap, not classification error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, confirmed random weight initialization, and comparisons isolating smaller models, early stopping or regularization. The experiment uses gated activations and greedy layerwise training.
ReLU teacher-student problems, joint teacher/student growth, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training degradation in plain batch-normalized networks and matched identity-shortcut comparisons.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature trajectories, recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified because R1–R3 lack readable training-accuracy values. Test accuracy and regularized optimality gaps cannot substitute for training classification error. The missing figure values concern existing rows, rather than omitted results.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization for the CIFAR-10 experiment, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and smaller models or early stopping are not tested. The training-accuracy values appear only in a figure.
